# Welcome

This site brings together practicals on comparative effectiveness with real-world data. Chapter 7 focuses on average treatment effects and propensity-score adjustment; Chapter 8 focuses on effect modification; Chapter 10 focuses on missing-data exploration and multiple imputation.

The practical collections include learner task pages; worked solutions are linked where available.

## Chapter 7: Confounding adjustment using propensity scores

Work through the practicals in sequence. They use a shared simulated cohort to estimate treatment effects using different propensity-score methods.

| Practical | Focus | Task | Worked solution |
|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline comparison and propensity-score estimation | Inspect the cohort, estimate propensity scores, and assess overlap and balance. | [Open the task](Chapter_7/chapter7_practical1_task.html) | [Open the solution](Chapter_7/chapter7_practical1_solution.html) |
| Propensity-score matching | Match participants and estimate the ATT. | [Open the task](Chapter_7/chapter7_practical2_task.html) | [Open the solution](Chapter_7/chapter7_practical2_solution.html) |
| Propensity-score stratification | Estimate treatment effects within propensity-score strata. | [Open the task](Chapter_7/chapter7_practical3_task.html) | [Open the solution](Chapter_7/chapter7_practical3_solution.html) |
| Propensity-score weighting | Estimate treatment effects with propensity-score weights. | [Open the task](Chapter_7/chapter7_practical4_task.html) | [Open the solution](Chapter_7/chapter7_practical4_solution.html) |
| Regression adjustment for the propensity score | Adjust the outcome model for the estimated propensity score. | [Open the task](Chapter_7/chapter7_practical5_task.html) | [Open the solution](Chapter_7/chapter7_practical5_solution.html) |

## Chapter 8: Effect modification in non-randomized studies

These six practicals use a companion multiple-sclerosis cohort to compare subgroup-specific treatment effects. The baseline data-generating process follows Chapter 3, while the treatment effect varies across five baseline Iscore groups so the methods can illustrate heterogeneity.

| Practical | Focus | Task |
|---|---|---|
| Introduction and exploration | Describe subgroup sizes, baseline balance, support, and crude outcome patterns. | [Open the practical](Chapter_8/chapter8_practical1_task.html) |
| Covariate adjustment | Estimate subgroup-specific effects with treatment-by-Iscore outcome regression. | [Open the practical](Chapter_8/chapter8_practical2_task.html) |
| Propensity-score matching | Match within Iscore groups and assess retention and balance. | [Open the practical](Chapter_8/chapter8_practical3_task.html) |
| Propensity-score weighting | Estimate subgroup-specific ATT weights and inspect ESS and balance. | [Open the practical](Chapter_8/chapter8_practical4_task.html) |
| Covariate adjustment for the propensity score | Compare continuous and categorical score adjustment. | [Open the practical](Chapter_8/chapter8_practical5_task.html) |
| Propensity-score stratification | Estimate treatment effects within score strata. | [Open the practical](Chapter_8/chapter8_practical6_task.html) |

## Chapter 10: Missing data

These practicals explore incomplete study data and use multiple imputation before estimating treatment effects.

Work through the activities in order: **Exploration** builds familiarity with the study data and missingness; **Multiple imputation** uses those findings to specify and assess an imputation model, then compares treatment-effect analyses.

| Practical | Focus | Task | Worked solution |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Exploration** | Understand the study variables, inspect missingness, and prepare for the analysis. | [Open the task](Chapter10/Practicals/chapter10_exploration_task.html) | [Open the solution](Chapter10/Practicals/chapter10_exploration_solution.html) |
| **Multiple imputation** | Impute missing data under a MAR model, check the imputation, pool treatment-effect estimates, and explore an MNAR sensitivity analysis for log medical cost. | [Open the task](Chapter10/Practicals/chapter10_homogeneous_treatment_effect_task.html) | [Open the solution](Chapter10/Practicals/chapter10_homogeneous_treatment_effect_solution.html) |

## Getting started

Install [R](https://cran.r-project.org/) and [RStudio](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/). Start with a practical's task page before opening its worked solution. The task pages include R code and instructions. Keep the supplied data files in the practical project directory when running the code locally.

The examples use observational data, so the results illustrate an analysis workflow and depend on the assumptions described in the practicals. In particular, multiple imputation does not by itself remove bias: the imputation model and assumptions about the missingness process matter.
